newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps climb - CFDs up 13 ct, mogas gains.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps climb - CFDs up 13 ct, mogas gains.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed on Friday, gaining further ground later.
Dealers said demand in Asia and a firmer tone on oil futures were behind the gains.
Brent crude CFDs gained 13 cts a barrel to around 48 cents under June for next week, although afternoon levels slipped a cent or two below the days highs.

The following three weeks were pegged around 45 cents under, 42 cents under and 34 cents respectively. Physical Brent gained ground with at least four of five Brents that turned wet being kept by the five o'clock deadline.
Heavy fuel climbed $2 a tonne to talk around $83.25 for May barges by the close. June was $1 higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade.
Low sulphur was valued around $88.50 for May but no trade was heard.

Gasoline rose $1 a tonne to $193.50 for May and $191 for June. Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were little changed with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent held at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat after edging higher on Thursday. May held around $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that levels on Thursday. The third and fourth quarters holding at $27.25 and $32 above the screen respectively.
